samples.summary: The new `isCellTable` heuristic is applied to the JSON import path too, silently changing where a JSON import lands (`--start` ignored) — a path no doc, skill or schema entry describes
samples.evidence: `sheets-import.ts:103` runs `isCellTable(rows)` on `rows` regardless of `fmt`. For `fmt === 'json'`, `rows` is synthesized at `sheets-import.ts:73-75` from an array of objects as `[Object.keys(objs[0]), ...values]` — and `sheets export <doc> out.json` / `GET .../cells` return objects keyed exactly `{ ref, value, formula, style }` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:60-64). So a JSON import that previously landed as a positional grid at `--start` now lands by reference at the exported refs, overwriting a different region of the target sheet. Every consumer-facing description of the switch is CSV-only: packages/cli/skills/sheets-import-export.md:51 ("A CSV whose header row is ..."), packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:565, docs/design/cli.md:935, and the `--start` help text at sheets-import.ts:48. Fix belongs either on the new code (gate `isCellTable` on `fmt === 'csv'`) or on the docs/schema.

samples.summary: Two backend contract changes break every already-published CLI against an upgraded server, with no version negotiation on the server side
samples.evidence: `CliExchangeDto.verifier` is now a required `@IsString() @Matches(...)` field, and `main.ts:65-72` runs `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })`, so an older CLI posting `{ code }` to `/auth/cli/exchange` gets a 400 that `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:76-81` surfaces only as "Token exchange failed.". Separately, `GET /auth/github?mode=cli` no longer redirects (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:48 + cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts), so an older CLI's opened URL renders a page whose Continue link it never follows, and its 30s wait times out. The new CLI carries an explicit diagnostic for the old-server direction (`REFUSAL.noState`), but nothing covers the old-CLI/new-server direction — worth an explicit note or a version hint in the 400 body.

samples.summary: `buildCellMap` now routes any `=`-leading cell text to `formula` for ALL grid imports (CSV and JSON), with no opt-out flag on the import side
samples.evidence: `csv-parse.ts:149` calls `toCellPatch`, which sends `=`-leading text as `{ formula }` (csv-parse.ts:90-92). Previously every grid cell was `{ value }`. Callers: `sheets-import.ts:107` for both CSV and JSON inputs. A pipeline that imported literal text beginning with `=` (a label column, a diff/log dump) now creates live formulas server-side; `--raw` exists only on `sheets export`, so there is no import-side escape hatch. Skills document the CSV case (packages/cli/skills/sheets-import-export.md:55) but not the JSON case, and neither mentions an opt-out.

verdict.reason: The finding's blocking rationale is that the JSON import path is undescribed ("a path no doc, skill or schema entry describes"; "Every consumer-facing description of the switch is CSV-only"). That is not present as described. registry.ts:565 states the switch as "Ignored when the input's first row is the per-cell header ref,value,formula[,style]" — format-agnostic; the --start help text at sheets-import.ts:48 says "ignored for an exported ref,value,formula table" with no mention of CSV; docs/design/cli.md:371-373 states it format-agnostically in the command tree; and the driving spec (20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:279-288) says "sheets-import.ts picks the branch" on input shape. So the JSON behaviour is inside the documented contract, and it is not silent — mode:'cells' is returned (sheets-import.ts:109,121-122) exactly so an inert --start is visible. Only skills/sheets-import-export.md:51 uses CSV-only prose, a minor wording narrowness. Blast-radius specifics also fail: I grepped every `sheets import` reference (recipe-csv-pipeline.md:25,52; developers/cli.md:326-341; docs/design/cli.md:547-551; scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md:15; files/upload.ts:35-36; cli tests) and no consumer imports JSON with --start or depends on the old grid placement of exported JSON, whose by-reference landing is the stated round-trip identity. The only remaining substance (heuristic false-positives) is statable without leaving sheets-import.ts:65-107 and belongs to the correctness lens.

finding.summary: Two backend contract changes break every already-published CLI against an upgraded server, with no version negotiation on the server side
finding.evidence: `CliExchangeDto.verifier` is now a required `@IsString() @Matches(...)` field, and `main.ts:65-72` runs `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })`, so an older CLI posting `{ code }` to `/auth/cli/exchange` gets a 400 that `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:76-81` surfaces only as "Token exchange failed.". Separately, `GET /auth/github?mode=cli` no longer redirects (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:48 + cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts), so an older CLI's opened URL renders a page whose Continue link it never follows, and its 30s wait times out. The new CLI carries an explicit diagnostic for the old-server direction (`REFUSAL.noState`), but nothing covers the old-CLI/new-server direction — worth an explicit note or a version hint in the 400 body.

verdict.reason: The DTO/pipe/middleware code is present as described, but the asserted impact path is guarded upstream and the asserted gap already exists in code. An older CLI sends no `challenge` (the current CLI adds it at packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:45-46), and the OAuth callback refuses a challenge-less CLI login before any code is minted, with an explicit browser-visible diagnostic: "CLI login is missing its proof-of-possession challenge. Update the wafflebase CLI and run `wafflebase login` again." (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:196-201). CliAuthStore.createCode requires a non-optional challenge (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts:129) and is only called after that guard (auth.controller.ts:202), so an old CLI never obtains a code and can never reach the required-`verifier` 400 that the finding says surfaces as the opaque "Token exchange failed." (login.ts:76-81). The finding's stated remedy — "an explicit note … for the old-CLI/new-server direction" — is exactly auth.controller.ts:196-201. The confirmation page's Continue link is followed by the human in the browser (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:175), not by the CLI, and the "30s wait" is not this tree's behaviour (login.ts:212 sets 180_000ms, and timeouts name the last refusal at login.ts:239-242). No in-repo consumer is left on the old contract: the only caller of /auth/cli/exchange posts {code, verifier} (login.ts:70-74). What remains is a nicer 400 body/version hint, which is minor and not a broken or bypassing call site under the blast-radius rubric.
